findings.label: Radiating eosinophilic clubs around colonies
findings.evidence: In-text: sulfur granules consisted of bacterial filaments bordered by eosinophilic Splendore-Hoeppli material; radiating eosinophilic material is visible.

panels.rationale: Single H&E histopathology image from a patient with abdominal actinomycosis. The image demonstrates sulfur granules with prominent radiating eosinophilic Splendore-Hoeppli material, supporting the disease attribution. [raw subtype: abdominal actinomycosis]
panels.attribution_text: Ayoub et al. Case Series of Abdominal Actinomycosis: An Old Diagnostic Conundrum.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.69763. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
in_text_mentions: her admission with a plan for a follow-up in the surgical outpatient clinic. On histology, "sulfur" granules were noticed; consisting of an irregularly rounded cluster of bacteria (filaments) bordered by eosinophilic, cube, and rectangular-like projections called a Splendore-Hoeppli material (Figure 3). Histology confirmed the diagnosis of abdominal actinomycosis. The patient completed a four-week course of oral antibiotics (amoxicillin 500 mg three times per day) as per the microbiologist's recommendation. She was later reviewed in the outpatient clinic and reported a good clinical response.
